title: The store schema is versioned; every schema change is a numbered forward-only migration committed in-tree
description: Schema evolution is expressed as an ordered catalog of numbered migrations. Each migration carries a monotonic version integer, a human description, and one or more DDL/data statements. The catalog lives in-tree next to the store code and is the sole source of schema truth; the store's current version is a fact recorded in a bookkeeping row inside the store itself and updated only by the migration runner.
rationale: A schema catalog committed in-tree makes deploys reproducible: the code that opens the store and the migrations it expects ship together in one commit. Numbered forward-only migrations avoid the two failure modes of ad-hoc schema drift (undocumented change, incompatible rollback). Bookkeeping inside the store means the fact of a version cannot desync from the tables the version describes.
